summary_html: Federal transparency statutes—**FOIA** and **Sunshine Act**—require disclosure of government data. Project Milk Carton promotes FOIA requests and public dashboards for child-welfare records.
authority_html:
- **Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552)** — public access to records  
- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Cincinnati Enquirer v. Jones-Kelley
key_cases.holding: The Court granted mandamus compelling the Department of Job and Family Services to release a requested database, holding the custodian failed to carry its burden of showing the records fell squarely within a statutory exception and that a later amendment excluding foster-caregiver information did not apply retroactively.
key_cases.relevance: This is the leading Ohio authority on public-records access to child-welfare agency data.
key_cases.quote: A custodian does not meet this burden if it has not proven that the requested records fall squarely within the exception.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Clough v. Franklin Cty. Children Servs.
key_cases.holding: The Court denied a parent's mandamus petition for her children-services file because the records are confidential by statute and she made no showing of good cause outweighing the confidentiality interest, and she could not seek records she had never requested before filing.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading Ohio decision on public-records and mandamus access to children-services records.
key_cases.quote: The good cause shown must outweigh the considerations underlying the confidentiality requirement.

key_cases.holding: County children services board investigation records kept under R.C. 5153.17 and 2151.141 are 'official records' subject to the sealing provisions of R.C. 2953.52, and the prosecutor who failed to object timely could not relitigate the sealing order later.
key_cases.relevance: Any transparency analysis of Ohio CPS records must start from this classification of R.C. 5153.17 files and the sealing regime attached to it.
key_cases.quote: records of a county children services board investigation made pursuant to R.C. 5153.17 and 2151.141 are "official records" within the ambit of the sealing provisions of R.C. 2953.52

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Cincinnati Enquirer v. Bloom
key_cases.holding: Interpreting the Ohio Constitution's open courts provision independently, the Court held that it creates a presumption of public access to juvenile delinquency proceedings which a statute cannot override, so a juvenile proceeding may not be closed without an individualized determination balancing the competing interests.
key_cases.relevance: This is the most recent and most significant Ohio transparency ruling on juvenile court proceedings.
key_cases.quote: the open courts provision provides a presumption of public access to juvenile delinquency proceedings

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Renfro v. Cuyahoga Cty. Dept. of Human Servs.
key_cases.holding: The Court denied mandamus to foster parents seeking a children services agency's child-abuse investigation report, holding that R.C. 2151.421 makes such reports confidential and removes them from R.C. 149.43, that they are exempt from R.C. 1347.08 as investigatory material compiled for law-enforcement purposes, and that the R.C. 5153.17 confidentiality duty — while not absolute — barred inspection absent an overriding right such as a parent's fair-trial interest.
key_cases.relevance: Any Ohio transparency analysis of children-services records starts here, with the three statutes — R.C. 149.43, 1347.08 and 5153.17 — that Renfro holds do not compel release.
key_cases.quote: keeping foster care records confidential, not disclosing them, is respondent's primary responsibility under the statute

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Scripps Howard Broadcasting Co. v. Cuyahoga Cty. Court of Common Pleas, Juv. Div.
key_cases.holding: The Court granted mandamus compelling a juvenile judge to release the transcript of a contempt proceeding held in his juvenile case, holding that the right of public access extends to transcripts as well as live proceedings and that Juv.R. 37(B) could not be applied to withhold the transcript without the findings required by In re T.R. that access could harm the child and that the harm outweighs the benefits of access.
key_cases.relevance: This is Ohio's pre-Bloom framework for public access to juvenile proceedings and their records, and it is the baseline against which Bloom's constitutional presumption must be measured.
key_cases.quote: The right of access includes both the live proceedings and the transcripts which document those proceedings.
